citeAs: Helber, P., Bischke, B., Dengel, A., Borth, D. (2019). EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth (German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI))
description: EuroSAT is a novel dataset for land use and land cover classification based on Sentinel-2 satellite images. It consists of 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches (64x64 pixels) covering 10 classes, with 13 spectral bands including visible, near-infrared, and shortwave-infrared. The dataset is distributed across European cities in over 34 countries and is made publicly available for Earth observation applications.
name: EuroSAT
publisher: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Image patches were labeled according to 10 land use and land cover classes (annual crop, permanent crop, pasture, highway, residential buildings, industrial buildings, river, sea & lake, forest, herbaceous vegetation) based on the European Urban Atlas mapping guide. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images were corrected or removed.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset covers European cities distributed over 34 countries, with distribution influenced by the number of cities per country represented in the European Urban Atlas, which may introduce geographic bias. Images were recorded throughout the year to maximize intra-class variance. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. Images with snow or ice were removed, which may reduce representation of winter conditions.
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were downloaded from the Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3. Images were selected from European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas, distributed over 34 European countries. Images with a low cloud level were selected. Images were recorded throughout the year to maximize variance in land use and land cover classes. From these satellite images, 27,000 georeferenced and labeled image patches (64x64 pixels) were created.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Satellite images with high cloud coverage were excluded by selecting images with a low cloud level value provided by ESA. Images containing snow or ice were identified and removed during manual checking. Images with dead pixels or mislabeling were also discarded.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral satellite images acquired by the Sentinel-2A satellite, covering 13 spectral bands (B01–B12 plus B08A) in the visible, near-infrared, and shortwave-infrared spectrum. Images were downloaded via Amazon S3 and are associated with European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images were extracted from recordings made throughout the year; the Sentinel-2A satellite was launched in June 2015. Application examples reference images from December 2015 through March 2017, indicating the collection spans at least this period.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The spatial resolution is 10 meters per pixel, which limits the granularity of classification compared to very-high-resolution datasets. The patch-based classification (64x64 pixels) does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The dataset is limited to European land cover classes as defined by the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from the satellite images. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice were removed. Bands with lower spatial resolution (20m or 60m per pixel) were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation for band evaluation experiments. The dataset was not atmospherically corrected.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables real-world Earth observation applications including monitoring deforestation (relevant to climate change), detecting illegal land use changes, urban development tracking, and assisting in keeping geographical maps up-to-date. It makes freely accessible Sentinel-2 satellite data usable for machine learning applications, potentially benefiting agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change research, and environmental monitoring.
rai:dataUseCases: Land use and land cover classification; land use and land cover change detection; assistance in keeping geographical maps (e.g., OpenStreetMap) up-to-date; Earth observation applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change monitoring, urban development, and environmental monitoring; training deep neural networks for satellite image classification.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify the number of independent annotations collected per image; images were manually checked but no per-item annotation count is given.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No information about annotator demographics is provided in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis are described.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No specific annotation platform is mentioned; annotation was done manually by the authors.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; missing/bad data was removed rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, balancing, resampling) of the dataset itself is described; upsampling of bands was only for evaluation experiments, not a dataset transformation.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of satellite images of land areas; no personal or sensitive information about individuals is collected.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine learning or automated tools were used in the annotation/labeling pipeline; labeling was done manually.
null_reasons.license: No license is explicitly stated in the paper, and the HuggingFace dataset entry also has no license listed.
